title: 建立 .NET 10 solution、模块项目与原生 CI 门禁
risks: The Windows and Ubuntu GitHub Actions matrix is defined but has not yet executed on remote runners; local evidence covers the Windows-equivalent command chain only.
The lexical duplicate-source and sensitive-log gates are intentionally conservative and will need controlled calibration as production source grows.
Integration, contract and migration suites do not exist in V01-001 because their production owners are not active; the current MSTest suite proves only the inert build foundation.
SDK roll-forward is disabled, so servicing updates require an explicit global.json and evidence refresh rather than an automatic upgrade.

reused_existing_logic: M0-009 validate_handoff.py, validate_architecture_baseline.py, verify_repository.py and CI tier contracts
NuGet central package management and committed lock-file mechanisms
new_language_or_framework: .NET SDK 10.0.111, runtime 10.0.11, net10.0, C# 14 and ASP.NET Core 10 activate the technology family already approved by ADR-0012
new_major_dependencies: Microsoft.AspNetCore.App 10 shared framework reference for the inert Core Server assembly
Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk 18.0.0, MSTest.TestAdapter 4.0.1 and MSTest.TestFramework 4.0.1 as test-only dependencies; 15-package locked closure, all MIT
contract_changes: Internal CI tier contract activates fail-closed .NET gates on Windows and Ubuntu fast-merge runners
Architecture baseline requires the root .NET build files, dependency/source gates and per-project lock files
architecture_tests: 19 repository tests including 11 .NET foundation and policy tests
NuGet source, SHA-512, license and vulnerability fail-closed fixtures
Duplicate-source, sensitive-log and CI continue-on-error fail-closed fixtures
git diff --check and Python cache-residue check
technical_debt: Run the new Windows and Ubuntu matrix remotely and retain its first CI evidence.
Add integration, public-contract and migration suites when their owning production tasks activate those behaviors.
Replace or calibrate lexical duplicate/log scanning only through reviewed policy changes once real-source evidence justifies it.
